verdict_task_A: No shared systematic found that could make a target-hosted signal look neighbour-hosted. The localisation conclusion (host = TIC 87055315 or a source within ~1" of it) survives; a PRF-free pixel test written for this audit independently rejects a target host. Verdict scale: supports false positive (for a planet on TIC 87055304). Some quoted significances are overstated (see statistics).
verdict_task_B: src/centroid.py could not exclude the neighbour: it is biased toward the aperture centre (positive-clipped flux-weighted centroid in an r = 3 px circle on the target), its S66 stack is dominated by two scattered-light windows, and its own sigma includes a 0.15 px floor. The ">6 sigma" exclusion divided the target-neighbour distance by the floor-free per-axis bootstrap error (err_px) and assumed an unbiased estimator; both are wrong.

pixel_test.definition: delta(p) = D(p)/O(p); Q = delta(x)/delta(y); H_target => Q = fT(x)/fT(y) <= 1/fT(y)

loc_independent.note: 0 of 20000 sims >= real: empirical p < 5e-5 (3.9 sigma) by count; >8 sigma relies on the Gaussian shape of the null far beyond the sampled range

psf_photometry.note: delta chi2 = 129 is a stat-only likelihood ratio (no PRF/registration systematic); with the adopted 0.07 systematic f_target = 1 is excluded at ~7.4 sigma
